jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Security Pricing and Packaging (Serverless) - Security Solutions
jobs.description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

 What is The Role

 We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to own how Elastic Security is packaged, priced, and sold on Elastic Cloud Serverless.

 More customers want to run SIEM, endpoint, and cloud security on Serverless, and the commercial model decides whether that growth is profitable. You will own the security solution layer on top of the Serverless platform: the tiers, the meters, the margins, and what it is like for a customer to pay for security on a consumption model. The Platform team owns the underlying architecture. You will work with them so that what we sell can be delivered at a healthy margin and quoted with confidence.

 We are changing how we price and package, and you will help design the new model. You own the pricing recommendation, and executive executive team makes the final call.

 The role sits between Product, Finance, Engineering, Sales, and Product Marketing. Expect to explain to a CISO, a CFO, and a field seller why a SKU looks the way it does.

 What You Will Be Doing

•
 Redesign how Security is packaged and priced on Serverless. Define the tiers, feature entitlements, and usage meters, select what is bundled, metered, or sold as an add-on, test the options against customer demand and COGS, and bring a recommendation to senior executive team.

•
 Own margin. Work with the Platform team and Finance to model the cost of new security capabilities, including ingest, search, retention, endpoint, and AI features, and set pricing requirements before a feature ships.

•
 Grow Security on Serverless from proof of concept to renewal. You are accountable for new workloads, migrations from hosted and self-managed deployments, expansion, and retention. Work with Finance to separate recurring growth from one-time proof-of-concept revenue.

•
 Give customers control over cost and performance. Define how search configurations, data tiers, and retention work for security use cases, and bring the cost models that justify new platform levers. Keep tenant-level packaging consistent with the Product Manager for MSSP and multi-tenancy.

•
 Simplify how customers understand cost. Cut packaging complexity first, then simplify the sizing and pricing estimators that customers and Solutions Architects use. Agree on a measure of "simple," such as time to a credible quote, and track it.

•
 Turn pricing decisions into shipped product. Write the PRDs and PRFAQs, and lead the work across Security engineering, the Serverless Platform team, Billing and Metering, and Cloud Operations. Help build the frameworks and reviews that other Security PMs, Product Marketing, and Solutions Architects use to price new capabilities.

•
 Stay close to the market and the field. Discuss with customers and prospects about what they will and won't pay for, track how other security platforms package and price, and help the field explain when Serverless, hosted, or self-managed is the right fit.

•
 You know the main approaches to pricing AI features, such as token-based, credit-based, and per-action or outcome pricing, and how inference costs and unpredictable usage shape each one.

 What You Bring

•
 You have led pricing and packaging for a SaaS or cloud product end to end, from option design and customer testing through margin modeling and executive approval, and you can point to the revenue, margin, or adoption result. Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing is required, as is experience simplifying a model that had grown too complex.

•
 Product experience with SIEM, XDR, endpoint, cloud security, or a security operations platform is a solid plus, and so is a background as a SOC analyst, detection engineer, or security architect. If your pricing work was on another cloud or data product, the team will help you learn the security side.

•
 You are comfortable with COGS, gross margin, and ARR modeling, and you can build a forecast with Finance without a translator.

•
 You understand how multi-tenant cloud services are built and how architecture choices drive cost, well enough to read a technical design.

•
 You lead through influence in a matrixed, remote-first company. You get enable teams to agree on a decision, work well asynchronously, and shift between priorities when the business changes.

•
 You can present pricing to a CISO and a procurement team, and you have supported deals

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager I, Base Pricing
jobs.description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

 Lyft connects people to transportation to change the way we live and get around our communities. We are looking for product managers who bring exceptional creative, strategic, and analytical skills to drive forward a best in class product. Product management at Lyft leads the integration of engineering, data science, and design to achieve the company's vision for reinventing transportation. We are looking for entrepreneurial and passionate Product Managers to innovate and execute across a rapidly growing, fast paced company and industry.

 Pricing is the primary economic engine of Lyft's marketplace — a high-precision, real-time system that processes millions of fare calculations per hour, balancing rider affordability, driver earnings, and Lyft's sustainable growth. The Pricing team sits at the intersection of the marketplace, mediating between rider demand and driver supply, and is a core pillar of the Rider Organization.

 The Base Pricing Team owns the systems that set the base price of a Lyft ride for every ride type, region, and ride intent. Behind these base prices is a machine-learning and optimization stack that predicts how the Lyft marketplace responds to price, translates the cost of serving a ride into a price, and recommends price changes across hundreds of markets every week. Base prices are the foundation of every fare, and they set the reference point that dynamic pricing and rider discounts build on.

 The team serves two sets of customers: riders, who should see prices that are fair, competitive, and matched to what they value; and the analysts and market managers who use our models and tools to set pricing strategy.

 Responsibilities:

 As the Staff Product Manager for Base Pricing, you will own the vision and roadmap for how Lyft sets base prices, and define the success metrics that measure it. That includes:

• Determining the optimal granularity at which Lyft sets base prices (e.g., by time, location, and type of trip)

• Improving how our base price optimization engine works with downstream dynamic pricing systems to better respond to real-time market conditions

• Re-evaluating how costs to fulfill a ride impact prices

• Jointly optimizing prices across ride types, so that standard, alternative modes, and scheduled rides are priced as one portfolio

• Making our impact estimation models accurate and trusted by market management teams

• Evolving base pricing to function in a hybrid network with autonomous vehicles

• Work closely with cross-functional stakeholders (engineers, scientists, analysts), and partner teams (Driver Earnings, Verticals, Market Management) to align on a shared vision, define requirements, and prioritize inbound requests.

• Communicate roadmaps, experiment results, and pricing decisions clearly to audiences from partner teams up to Lyft's executive team.

 Experience:

• 5+ years of product management or relevant experience, with significant time spent on algorithmic, data-driven, pricing, or marketplace products

• A deep technical understanding of microeconomics, and ideally a background in Operations Research, Econometrics, Machine Learning, or algorithmic systems

• Experience owning pricing, revenue management, or other economic levers with direct P&L impact; experience with price optimization, elasticity modeling, or cost modeling is a strong plus

• Experience running A/B tests and market-level experiments, using statistical and causal inference techniques to evaluate results, and developing post-launch testing strategies

• Experience with data, including querying, aggregation, analysis, and visualization; comfortable working directly in SQL and with data science partners on model design

• Ability to define and analyze metrics that inform the success of products, and excellent judgment about the dynamics of a product ecosystem

• Natural ability to make things happen around you; you manage ambiguity, complexity, and interdependencies across many teams in an organized and structured way

• Strong communication skills and intuition for communication strategy at every level — within teams, within the company, and with executives

• Passion for Lyft and what we are trying to achieve in sustainable urban transportation

 Benefits:

• Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled

• Mental health benefits

• Family building benefits

• Child care and pet benefits

• 401(k) plan with company match to help save for your future

• In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off, hourly team members have 15 days paid time off

• 18 weeks of paid parental leave. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible

• Subsidized commuter benefits

• Monthly Lyft credits and complimentary

jobs.title: Director, Pricing & Packaging
jobs.description:
WHAT IS BOX?

 Box (NYSE:BOX) is the leader in Intelligent Content Management. Our platform enables organizations to fuel collaboration, manage the entire content lifecycle, secure critical content, and transform business workflows with enterprise AI. We help companies thrive in the new AI-first era of business. Founded in 2005, Box simplifies work for leading global organizations, including JLL, Morgan Stanley, and Nationwide. Box is headquartered in Redwood City, CA, with offices across the United States, Europe, and Asia.

 By joining Box, you will have the unique opportunity to continue driving our platform forward. Content powers how we work. It’s the billions of files and information flowing across teams, departments, and key business processes every single day: contracts, invoices, employee records, financials, product specs, marketing assets, and more. Our mission is to bring intelligence to the world of content management and empower our customers to completely transform workflows across their organizations. With the combination of AI and enterprise content, the opportunity has never been greater to transform how the world works together and at Box you will be on the front lines of this massive shift.

 WHY BOX NEEDS YOU

 Box is evolving in terms of pricing and packaging – taking our more straightforward, seat-based model and augmenting it with API-call-base and AI-driven consumption. The Director, Pricing & Packaging will help Box navigate the shift from traditional enterprise software pricing towards consumption-based pricing tied to AI usage, units, platform activity, costs, and business value.

 The impact of this leader will be both strategic and operational. They will bring analytical rigor to pricing model design while helping cross-functional teams align around recommendations, tradeoffs, and implementation. Success will depend not only on building the right model, but also on clearly articulating the business context and strategy behind pricing recommendations to senior leaders.

 This is an individual contributor role reporting into our Vice President, Product Marketing. This role will be hybrid based in our Redwood City, CA global HQ three days per week.

 YOUR IMPACT AT BOX

 The Director, Pricing & Packaging will own a strategic and execution-oriented pricing function focused on helping Box modernize its pricing approach. Key responsibilities include:

•
 Lead the evolution of Box’s pricing model from a primarily seat-based approach to more complex platform, usage, and AI consumption-based models.

•
 Develop pricing models for AI usage and consumption units that make sense for Box’s business as the traditional seat-unit model becomes less central.

•
 Partner closely with key stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Finance, Controllership, GTM, and executive leadership to roll out pricing models that are analytically sound and commercially viable.

•
 Build rigorous pricing analyses using strong quantitative skills, including modeling, spreadsheets, regression, intake analysis, cost considerations, and business-case development.

•
 Translate complex pricing work into a clear business story that helps executives and partner teams understand the recommendation, rationale, tradeoffs, and expected impact.

•
 Operate effectively in ambiguity, bringing structure to complex, evolving problems where the path forward may not yet be fully defined.

•
 Drive alignment and implementation, not just strategy, by working through operational challenges, influencing cross-functional teams, and bringing stakeholders along.

•
 Understand and articulate how AI models are priced, why those pricing structures matter, and how they affect Box’s business economics.

 WHO YOU ARE

 Box executives are engaged, passionate leaders who prioritize customer centricity, innovation, and growth. As an AI-first company, XLT members bring a growth mindset and proactively leverage AI to make faster, smarter decisions that amplify their impact across the business.

 As a leader in this role, you have/are:

•
 Highly quantitative skill set, including comfort with pricing modeling, spreadsheets, regression, cost analysis, and structured business analysis.

•
 Strong pricing and packaging expertise, ideally in enterprise SaaS, AI, platform pricing, or usage-based pricing environments.

•
 Strong understanding of AI-related pricing dynamics, including how AI models are priced, why those pricing structures matter, and how they affect business economics.

•
 Ability to do the analytical work directly, not only manage or advise on it.

•
 Strong storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to articulate pricing recommendations clearly to executives and cross-functional partners.

•
 Influence and stakeholder-management skills, especially in ambiguous situations where teams may have competing priorities or resistance to change.

•
 Ability to operationalize strategy, ensuring recommendations move beyond a deck

 About the team

 Revenue Operations is a small team with outsized reach. Deal Desk is the part of RevOps closest to the deal: we help reps structure pricing, build quotes, and move contracts through approval so they can close faster without giving away margin. As Alloy sells into more banks, credit unions, fintechs, and channel partners, more deals come through the desk every quarter, and they're getting more varied. This role reports to the Senior Revenue Operations Manager, Deal Desk, and will be the second person on the desk.

 Alloy operates in a hybrid-work environment. We look to foster collaboration and community by having our local employees onsite three days a week.

 What you'll be doing

 You'll be the first stop for reps working through the mechanics of a deal: building and checking quotes, keeping the approval queue moving, and making sure what gets signed is what gets booked and billed. It's a high-volume, detail-heavy seat with a front-row view of how Alloy prices, packages, and contracts, and a lot of room to make the process better as you learn it.

• Partner with our Systems and Salesforce admins to improve CPQ and quoting workflows: flag where reps get stuck, document requirements for fixes and enhancements, test changes before they go live, and update guides once they ship.

• Review closed-won contracts for booking accuracy (ACV, CARR, term, billing frequency, uplifts) and keep the bookings tracker current.

• Pull weekly reporting on deals in flight, request volume, turnaround time, and discount and approval trends.

• Help maintain CPQ, Ironclad, and Deal Desk process, and turn repeat questions into documentation (CPQ Handbook)

• 1-3 years in Deal Desk, Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Order Management, or a similar analytical role supporting a sales team.

• Hands on Salesforce experience with opportunities, quotes, and reports.

• Salesforce CPQ (or similar) experience.

• Interest in automating manual deal desk work.

• Strong Excel and Google Sheets skills.

• Sharp attention to detail, with a habit of catching the wrong date or mismatched number before it reaches a customer.

• Comfort working a queue: many requests at once, prioritized by deadline, with people kept informed along the way.

• Clear, direct written communication, including explaining a policy to a rep or saying "not yet" without creating friction.

• Curiosity about how deals work, from pricing and contract terms to how they flow into bookings and billing.

• Experience with Ironclad or another contract lifecycle management tool.

• Experience gathering requirements or testing changes for a CRM or quoting tool.

• Experience in B2B SaaS, fintech, or financial services.

• Familiarity with SaaS metrics and deal terms such as ARR, CARR, usage-based pricing, ramps, and multi-year uplifts.

• Exposure to order forms, billing, or revenue recognition basics (ASC 606).

• Familiarity with SQL.

jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

 About the Product Team

 The Product team listens to our customers’ needs and translates those insights into a clear product vision. The team works closely with design, engineering, and analytics to build scalable financial products that empower people to manage their money with confidence. We rely on empathy, curiosity, and business sense to prioritize features and improve experiences. Our role is to lead with clarity, support cross-functional execution, and champion the user in every decision.

 As a Staff Product Manager on Affirm’s Credit & Pricing team, you’ll shape how consumers discover, understand, and use available credit. You’ll own the strategy for credit experiences spanning shopping, repayment, and marketing, turning complex credit capabilities into intuitive products that build trust and drive activation, conversion, and repeat engagement.

 What You'll Do

• Set the product direction. Define a cohesive vision for consumer credit experiences, identify the most valuable problems to solve, and translate your strategy into priorities across multiple teams.

• Build experiences that make credit understandable. Help consumers explore potential financing options before checkout, discover where they have purchasing power, and understand when credit becomes available again after repayment.

• Create more relevant consumer journeys. Develop personalized experiences for new and returning consumers, using research and experimentation to determine what information, guidance, and next steps best meet their needs.

• Connect platform capabilities to consumer outcomes. Own merchant prequalification and purchasing power experiences, partnering with core purchasing power and credit decisioning teams to translate underlying capabilities into clear, consistent experiences.

• Lead consequential product decisions. Bring Engineering, Design, Analytics, Credit, Marketing, Commercial, and Legal partners together to resolve tradeoffs across consumer needs, growth, risk, and partner commitments. Influence senior leaders through clear recommendations and sound judgment.

• Own measurable results. Define success, lead discovery and experimentation, and use funnel analysis and consumer feedback to improve activation, purchase conversion, repeat engagement, and comprehension while supporting responsible access to credit.

 What We Look For

• A record of building impactful consumer products. 7+ years of product management experience, with demonstrated success taking products from discovery through launch and scaling adoption in fintech, e-commerce, marketplaces, or similarly complex environments.

• Leadership across teams. Experience independently setting direction for a substantial product area, influencing senior stakeholders, and aligning multiple teams around priorities and measurable outcomes.

• Strong consumer product judgment. An ability to translate complex systems into intuitive experiences, with a high bar for interaction design, clear communication, and consumer trust.

• Strategic and technical depth. You connect long-term opportunities to practical product and platform decisions, and work effectively with engineers on capabilities that serve multiple experiences.

• Analytical and experimental rigor. You combine customer research, behavioral data, and well-designed experiments to prioritize opportunities, evaluate tradeoffs, and decide what to scale, change, or stop.

• Ownership in ambiguity. You bring structure to open-ended problems, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and communicate the rationale, risks, and support needed to move forward.

• Relevant domain curiosity. Experience with credit, lending, personalization, or AI-powered consumer experiences is a plus. You can learn complex domains quickly and distinguish useful innovation from technology without a clear customer need.

We are committed to building a data-centric and AI-augmented Deal Desk that leverages predictive analytics and automated workflows to optimize pricing in real-time and automate routine approvals, allowing for deeper strategic focus.

 Available Location: Singapore

 Role Summary

 As a Deal Desk Manager, you will be the architect of our AI-driven deal desk, transitioning our sales process from manual workflows to an intelligent, automated engine that spans from initial scoping to final execution. Identify bottlenecks and implement AI-powered productivity solutions.

• Drive Process Iteration: Partner with cross-functional teams (Legal, Finance, Product) to build, streamline, and automate deal desk processes, architecting autonomous approval workflows and focusing on reducing field friction through relentless automation.

• Minimum 8+ years of Deal Desk, FP&A, Revenue Operations, or similar experience with a proven track record supporting large-scale enterprise sales motions; 3+ years of direct deal desk experience (deal analysis, deal governance and customer negotiation) preferred

• Financial & Sales Acumen: Solid understanding of SaaS metrics, pricing models, and financial concepts like ARR, Gross Margin, churn, and profitability. Experience with revenue recognition principles (e.g., ASC 606) is highly desirable. Experience selling software is a bonus

As the most trusted global leader in data-first contract lifecycle management (CLM) software, Agiloft helps organizations manage the end-to-end process of proposing, negotiating, signing, and leveraging contracts using our flexible Data-first Agreement Platform (DAP). With contract data as the foundation, customers quickly and collaboratively reach agreement and leverage contract visibility to thrive with competitive advantage. Employing powerful, pragmatic artificial intelligence as a legal force multiplier, and robust integration capabilities as a data liberator, organizations around the world trust Agiloft’s certified implementers to deliver connected, intelligent, and autonomous solutions across the entire contract lifecycle.

Top analysts like Gartner, Forrester, and IDC agree, all showing Agiloft as a leader in the CLM space. Our no code platform is easily managed and administered by business users, which is why Agiloft is the contract you keep: nearly a full 100% of new customers are satisfied with their initial implementations, and some 97% of customers renew every year. Ours is a growing, vibrant, successful company that is at the forefront of a market that is becoming a must-have for all organizations.

We believe that the way to build the strongest, most vibrant place to work is to bring in individuals from all walks of life, and to support them in bringing their authentic selves to their day, every day. Our working philosophy is that “EX = CX”: when employee experience is excellent, so is customer experience. We support multiple Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), and offer a working environment that supports healthy work/life balance, including floating holidays and a quarterly, no-questions-asked wellness day.


Position Overview
Agiloft is building new paths to monetize the value it creates, including new consumption and outcome-based models, and we need dedicated ownership of the analytical and operational engine behind that work. The Pricing & Packaging Manager will be responsible for developing and putting forward the recommendations to the pricing committee for review and approval regarding pricing research, model design(s), packaging analysis, and monetization experiments that directly inform how Agiloft goes to market.
This role sits within the Product organization, reporting to the Director of Product GTM, and works in close partnership with Finance, Sales, Revenue Operations, and Product. You are the person who turns pricing questions into frameworks and frameworks into decisions that deliver customer solutions as transactable units of value that serve them and grow our business. You will build the quantitative foundation that allows Agiloft to deploy pricing as a strategic capability across functional boundaries.

jobs.title: Pricing & Order Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

 About Us

 Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on. Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

 As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on both companies' strengths while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact. During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

 About the Role

 Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies.

 We’re looking for a Pricing & Order Operations Analyst to join our Order Operations & Monetization team. This role restores dedicated capacity for pricing and order operations testing, quote-to-cash (QTC) release validation, and order execution support.

 You’ll help ensure system changes are tested, validated, and operationally ready before they go live. You’ll provide Pricing and Order Operations subject-matter expertise and execute assigned business validation across signature packets, bookings, marketplace offers, and booking-to-order management handoffs. This role partners closely with Order Operations & Monetization, IT’s business systems team, Pricing Operations, Sales, and Deal Desk.

 Reporting & Prioritization

• Reports to the Order Operations & Monetization lead, Jamie Calkins.

• The Senior Pricing Operations Manager may help prioritize pricing-related test cases and QTC issues tied specifically to pricing and quoting.

• The Order Operations & Monetization lead owns final prioritization of the analyst’s workload across order operations, assigned non-pricing UAT participation, and pricing-related support work .

 This is a hybrid role, 1-2 days in the office.

 Technologies You’ll Use

• Salesforce CPQ

• Jira

• Suger and marketplace user interfaces, including AWS, Azure, GCP, and Snowflake

• Notion

• Metronome

• Hex

 What You’ll Do

 Pricing Operations & QTC Support

• Support pricing operations changes through business requirement review, data validation, configuration checks, and documentation, helping ensure pricing logic is accurately reflected in QTC workflows.

• Validate pricing-related QTC changes across quoting, approvals, discounting logic, product configuration, and downstream order execution.

• Help confirm that pricing changes are operationally ready before launch, including impacts to Sales, Deal Desk, Order Operations, Billing, Revenue, and marketplace workflows.

• Partner with the Senior Pricing Operations Manager to prioritize pricing-related test cases, identify gaps in business requirements, and document expected system behavior.

• Help maintain documentation for pricing- and order-related system configurations, known dependencies, and release-readiness criteria.

 UAT & Testing

• Participate as a Pricing and Order Operations subject-matter expert in UAT project-managed by Technical Program Management (TPM) and executed under RevOps coordination, ensuring relevant business scenarios and expected outcomes are represented.

• Execute assigned Pricing and Order Operations test cases and collaborate with the GTM subject-matter experts identified by RevOps.

• Partner with RevOps and relevant subject-matter experts to develop and maintain Pricing and Order Operations test cases, including scenarios for quoting, approvals, signature packets, bookings, marketplace offers, billing, and order management.

• Document test results and defects with clear traceability from business requirement to test outcome, and provide domain-specific readiness input through the established UAT sign-off process.

• Maintain the Pricing and Order Operations portion of the regression test suite for recurring QTC changes.

 Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

 The Global Pricing Operations Team

 The Pricing Operations team works in a cross-functional, fast-paced, and dynamic environment with many moving pieces and evolving business needs. The team partners with Pricing Strategy Managers, Product Managers, Technology, Data & Intelligence, and various GTM teams to ensure Okta is operationally ready to bring new product pricing, buying programs, and strategic monetization initiatives to market.

 The Pricing Operations Principal Opportunity

 Okta is seeking a Pricing Operations Principal to lead initiatives that transform Okta's pricing strategy into successful go-to-market execution. A successful person in this role will be a strong collaborator, intensely curious, and supremely organized. They are known for connecting the dots, simplifying complexities, communicating clearly and proactively, and driving highly collaborative efforts to completion, even when the path forward isn't perfectly defined.

 In this role, you will serve as an operational leader for new pricing launches and a strategic buying-program implementation, establishing the integrated roadmap, operating cadence, decision-making framework, readiness criteria, and stakeholder communications required to bring these initiatives from concept through launch and sustained adoption. You will partner closely with senior cross-functional leaders to make complex tradeoffs, resolve dependencies, and ensure the business is ready to sell, quote, contract, provision, bill, recognize revenue, support, and renew under the new model.

Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities.  About Connect

 While accepting payments on the internet has become easier over the past several years, due in large part to the advent of modern payments APIs, the internet infrastructure for routing these same payments—to suppliers, sellers, partners, service providers, and recipients—remains outdated.

 Connect is Stripe’s leading product for marketplaces, on-demand services, ecommerce site builders, invoicing platforms, professional SaaS products, fundraising platforms, rental management platforms, and more. By using Connect, users in each of these categories can link multiple parties to exchange goods or services.
